chunks.rationale: .github/workflows/test.yml: libasound2 -> libasound2t64 in the smoke job's apt install. ubuntu-latest is now noble (24.04), where libasound2 is a virtual package with no installation candidate — every PR's smoke (ubuntu-latest) job failed at the apt step with exit 100 before the app ever started. The t64 suffix is the noble package name; the sibling libs (libatk1.0-0 etc.) still resolve via transitional dummy packages, so only libasound2 needed the rename.
risks: If GitHub ever points ubuntu-latest back at 22.04 (jammy), libasound2t64 does not exist there and the step breaks again — acceptable, ubuntu-latest only moves forward.

chunks.rationale: src/index.css: --text-dim #667085 -> #7d8798. The sidebar (projects/threadbar) renders most secondary text (branch names, ages, counts, provider tags, 'New thread' rows, group summaries) in --text-dim, which sat at ~3.7:1 contrast on --bg-elevated — below WCAG AA. The new value lands ~5:1 on the sidebar background and ~4.7:1 on card fills, while staying clearly darker than --text-muted (#8b95a8, ~6:1) so the dim/muted/text hierarchy survives. Token-level fix beats per-rule overrides in Sidebar.module.css: one line, no hardcoded colors, and other dim text app-wide benefits too.
risks: Dim text everywhere in the app gets brighter, not just the sidebar — intentional, but reviewers should confirm the dim/muted steps still read as distinct.
Settled rows still multiply the token by opacity 0.6 (intentional recession); they improve but remain low-contrast by design.
Merge with origin/main conflicted only on .solenta/review-itinerary.json (every thread writes it); resolved keeping this PR's version.

The 6 electron-suite test failures on this PR's checks (runner verification gate, auto-checkpoint, package-app.sh) are pre-existing main breakage tracked in #536 — they reproduce without this diff and are out of scope here.
Contrast ratios were computed analytically from hex values, not measured in a running app; local test run was not possible (worktree has no node_modules).
